$comment: Content excluded from the corpus, with the reason. The index builder skips these; NOTICE lists them. This is where a vendored skill goes when it cannot be made to satisfy the corpus constraints without rewriting it beyond recognition.

entries.name: fal-ai-media
entries.detail: The skill is a guide to fal.ai's hosted generation endpoints (Veo, Kling, Seedance, Nano Banana) and ElevenLabs. Those are paid, hosted AI generation services, which the corpus excludes: it covers open-source and local-hostable tools only.

entries.name: videodb
entries.detail: VideoDB is a hosted SaaS. The skill documents its cloud API (ingest, index, transcode, generate) and there is no self-hosted or open-source path documented, so following it requires an account and a paid subscription. The local equivalents for the operations it covers live in media-transcode-pipeline, subtitle-generation, video-editing, audio-separation, and local-diffusion-suite.

entries.name: email
entries.detail: The skill documents Resend, a hosted transactional-email service, and its templates, with a workflow specific to Vercel deployments. It teaches one paid SaaS rather than the category, and requires an account and an API key. For sending mail from a local or self-hosted stack, see email-ops.

entries.name: social-publisher
entries.detail: The skill documents SocialClaw, a hosted workspace service reached through a workspace API key, which performs the publishing on SocialClaw's side. It is a hosted dependency rather than a local tool. The corpus's authored social-publish-scheduling skill covers planning and scheduling a campaign without a hosted publisher.
